newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end down 2.44 percent on stronger yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end down 2.44 percent on stronger yen.

text.p: Tokyo's main stock index closed down 2.44 percent on Friday due to profit taking in some export-orientated blue chips after the yen gained against the dollar in the afternoon session, brokers said.
NTT dragged other communications firms, such as DDI Corp with it. DDI finished 38,000 yen lower at 727,000.

In spite of the heavy losses, market sources said there was little fear of a free fall as the end of the business year was drawing near. A sharp plunge would shrink the value of stocks held by firms and hurt their earnings. "The downside is seen at the 25-day moving average level, which is at 18,385 today," one strategist said.
However, the Nikkei benchmark was also seen capped firmly at the 19,200-19,300 level.

Personal loan and credit firms were dampened by a recent cut in the rating of Credit Saison Co Ltd as well as speculation about heightening competition. Credit Saison fell 30 yen to 2,570. Promise Co Ltd shed 450 yen to 5,100 and was the fourth largest percentage loser on the Tokyo bourse. Acom Co Ltd lost 250 yen to 4,700.

By sector, issues that declined were led by mining, warehousing, credit/lease, communications and paper/pulp. Those that advanced were led by air transportation, railway/bus, land transportation, insurance and electric power.
The broader TOPIX index dropped 22.80 points, or 1.61 percent, to end at 1,390.59. The Nikkei 300 closed down 5.32 points, or 1.96 percent, at 265.93.
The second-section index tumbled 8.80 points, or 0.51 percent, to 1,726.26. Turnover was 8.18 million compared to 7.10 million on Thursday.
The over-the-counter index was also down in late trade, standing at 1,197.89 after losing 9.00 points, or 0.75 percent. -- Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9052
